name: Rigid-Column Pipe Flow with Darcy-Weisbach Friction
description: Source reconstruction of the single rigid-column momentum balance in Kruisbrink (1996), equation9.66,p.138, with constant boundary head100m, zero valve/minor loss, existing pipe dimensions and kinematic viscosity. Q is volumetric flow, so Q-prime equals area times force/mass. Pressure_Loss is instantaneous Darcy-Weisbach head loss, not head depletion; reservoir storage geometry is not modeled. Smooth-pipe friction follows EPA SWMM Hydraulics (2017), equations7-32/7-33,p.140, with linear transition between Re2000 and4000; zero roughness is the explicit hydraulically smooth idealization already implicit in the former Blasius correlation. The laminar force is evaluated as8*pi*rho*nu*L*V, including its exact zero-flow limit, rather than dividing by zero or flooring Re. Friction_Factor is a report with its undefined-at-rest state explicit. Viscous_Diffusion_Length=sqrt(nu*t) is only a diffusion-scale diagnostic, not a solved boundary-layer thickness. The former capped thickness integrator was unsupported. This educational incompressible, quasi-steady-friction approximation excludes waterhammer and the exact radial Navier-Stokes startup profile.

variables.name: Friction Factor
variables.equation: IF(Reynolds_Number == 0, 'Undefined at rest; friction force limit is zero', IF(Reynolds_Number <= 2000, 64 / Reynolds_Number, IF(Reynolds_Number < 4000, (0.032 + (Reynolds_Number - 2000) * (0.25 / (LN(5.74 / 4000^0.9) / LN(10))^2 - 0.032) / 2000), 0.25 / (LN(5.74 / Reynolds_Number^0.9) / LN(10))^2)))

variables.name: Friction Force
variables.equation: IF(Reynolds_Number <= 2000, 8 * 3.14159 * 1000 * Kinematic_Viscosity * Pipe_Length * Velocity, IF(Reynolds_Number < 4000, (0.032 + (Reynolds_Number - 2000) * (0.25 / (LN(5.74 / 4000^0.9) / LN(10))^2 - 0.032) / 2000), 0.25 / (LN(5.74 / Reynolds_Number^0.9) / LN(10))^2) * 1000 * Velocity * ABS(Velocity) * 3.14159 * Pipe_Diameter * Pipe_Length / 8)

variables.name: Diffusion Length Growth
variables.equation: IF(TIME == 0, 'Singular derivative at startup', 0.5 * SQRT(Kinematic_Viscosity / TIME))

reference: Kruisbrink ACH (1996), The dynamic behaviour of check valves in pipeline systems. City University London PhD thesis,p.138,equation9.66. Rossman LA (2017), EPA/600/R-17/111, SWMM Reference ManualII Hydraulics,p.140,equations7-32/7-33: https://nepis.epa.gov/Exe/ZyPURL.cgi?Dockey=P100S9AS.txt
